title: School district mill levy override big local election winner
copy: Telluride's school district mill levy override (5A) passed with 61.45% of the vote — 1,988 yes to 1,247 no — securing continued local funding to offset reductions from the state's new school funding formula. San Miguel County also elected a new sheriff, Lane Masters, over incumbent Dan Covault, 54–46%, and unaffiliated candidate Dylan Brooks won the county commissioner race over Democrat Paul Reich, 53–47%.

title: Lady Miners survive league tourney losses
copy: Telluride's Lady Miners went 0-2 at the San Juan Basin League Tournament, falling to Dolores (25-21, 25-12, 25-17) and Ignacio, but held their own enough to keep their postseason alive. They came out of the weekend ranked No. 36 in the 2A state field — right on the bubble — and earned a spot in regionals.

title: Telluride cross-country girls place 14th at State
copy: Telluride's girls cross-country team finished 14th at the CHSAA Class 2A State Championships in Colorado Springs, posting a team score of 212 points. Junior Liv Speck, the team's top runner, had to withdraw near the three-mile mark after feeling ill. Senior Ruby Cieciuch led the finishers in 21:54, placing 47th.

title: Spectacular spooky season
copy: Telluride marked Halloween with its annual Witches' Ride on Oct. 29 — costumed cyclists rolling through town — followed by the Halloween Parade down Colorado Avenue on Oct. 30. Both events drew the usual mix of kids and adults.

title: BOCC votes on oil and gas rules
copy: San Miguel County commissioners approved new Land Use Code amendments covering oil and gas, deep geothermal, and forestry operations. Oil and gas setbacks increase from 1,500 to 2,000 feet; no new local drilling permits have been issued since around 2011. Deep geothermal rules — new to the code — set 1,000-foot residential setbacks.

title: Bodies of 2 students are recovered after they died on hiking trip
copy: Two Colorado Mountain College students, Kaden Matsuda, 19, of Ridgway, and Jackson Donlon, 20, of New York, died during a backcountry trip after a severe storm dropped two feet of snow in the San Isabel area. Their bodies were recovered from a basin on West Apostle Mountain. The sheriff noted they were well-prepared — the mountains don't always care.

title: Heavy precipitation pulls San Juans out of drought
copy: October storms pulled most of San Miguel County out of drought, with the San Juan Mountains recording the highest rainfall accumulation in Colorado. The San Miguel River hit 1,600 cfs on Oct. 22 — a record for that date — and saturated soils heading into winter is considered a good sign for spring runoff. That said, four of the top 10 driest years on record have come in the past eight years, and one wet fall doesn't erase what farmers and ranchers have already lived through.

title: Bee ready for this buzzy event
copy: Wilkinson Public Library is hosting an Adult Spelling Bee at The Alibi on Friday, Nov. 6, 6:30–8:30 p.m. Teams are full but a waitlist is open, and spectators are welcome — audience participation is part of the plan. The Alibi is offering honey-themed drinks with a 10% discount for library cardholders.

title: CDOT seeks input on Sawpit, Placerville projects
copy: CDOT has $250,000 allocated for multimodal improvements in Sawpit and Placerville, with funds needing to be spent by 2030. Residents and commissioners discussed options like re-striping Highway 145 to narrow lanes and slow traffic, improving bus stops, and basic maintenance like ditch mowing. Engineers will review the feedback and return to the BOCC early next year.

title: Busy, busy at One to One Mentoring
copy: One to One Mentoring has a new case manager, Kelsey Brax, a former teacher who moved to Telluride in 2018. The program is also seeing mentor demand outpace supply — a familiar small-town stretch. Kate Greubel, an active mentor since 2022, recently stepped in as interim board president.

title: Upcoming youth events
copy: Late October and early November are busy for local youth sports and school events — basketball, volleyball, football, cross country, and Knowledge Bowl all on the schedule, plus Family-Teacher conferences Oct. 29–30 and a Halloween Carnival Oct. 31, 3–5 p.m.

title: Where art meets community
copy: The Telluride Wheelhouse, a 2,000-sq-ft community art studio in Ilium, has been run by Rob Nealan since late 2024. It offers ceramics, darkroom, letterpress, sewing, and open studio space, with memberships starting at $75/month. Nealan says prices haven't risen since he took over and space is available now.

title: Commissioners approve funding request from West End Family Link
copy: West End Family Link Center in Nucla, which serves roughly 2,170 residents across a wide stretch of Montrose and San Miguel Counties, closed in August due to budget shortfalls before reopening with $75,000 in emergency Montrose County funding. San Miguel County commissioners unanimously approved an additional $12,000 request to help cover operating costs and food pantry needs. The pantry has seen a 35% jump in demand from Norwood residents and delivers about 75 boxes monthly to homebound individuals — now running on a staff of three, down from seven.

title: CHALKBOARD
copy: Local birthdays and recurring community events for the Norwood and Nucla-Naturita area, including food pantry Sundays, senior meals Mondays and Thursdays, pickleball, AA meetings, free legal aid, and monthly board meetings for town, school, chamber, and parks. Contact details and schedules included.

title: Commissioners approve forestry practices amendment
copy: San Miguel County updated its Land Use Code to regulate forestry practices, requiring applicants to submit reports detailing project impacts and mitigation plans. The rules cover wildfire, wildlife, wetlands, and geologic hazards, with a threshold of 80+ acres or 1.5+ acres of disturbance triggering formal review. Most logging here is wildfire mitigation, not commercial.

title: Pioneer Day celebrations
copy: Norwood fifth graders took top honors at the Pioneer Day parade on Sept. 26, winning first place and Best Overall Float — along with $75 toward a pizza or ice cream party. Kids also took part in sack races as part of the annual celebration.

title: A life of service
copy: Norwood's Veterans Day ceremony traces back to 1999, when Nancy Wells and Karen Gauvey organized the first one after no other group stepped up. Wells, a former teacher, firefighter, and one of Philmont Scout Ranch's first two women rangers, has kept it going for 25 years. The school holds its annual assembly Nov. 11 at 9:30 a.m.

title: Legals and Public Notices for Oct. 29-Nov. 4, 2026
copy: The Tomboy Lodge HOA has filed a foreclosure action against a unit at 619 W. Columbia Ave. (Unit 156A) over an unpaid balance of $15,449.81. A sheriff's sale is scheduled for December 16, 2026, on the courthouse steps.

title: Michael Fagan
copy: Michael Fagan, who built his life and real estate appraisal career in Telluride after college, passed away August 29 at 76. He was remembered by friends for his skiing, his laugh, and his steady presence in the community. He is survived by his son Sean, daughter-in-law Aimee, and grandson Enzo.

title: Miner Volleyball takes two of Homecoming three
copy: Telluride volleyball swept Homecoming week with two wins, including a hard-fought 25-22, 26-28, 25-19, 25-21 victory over Crested Butte, moving the Lady Miners to 11-10 overall and up to no. 35 in state rankings. The boys soccer team dropped a 1-0 decision to Crested Butte on a deflected goal but still earned the no. 1 seed in the 2A State Tournament.

title: Shrek-tastic
copy: "Shrek the Musical" ran at the Sheridan Opera House Oct. 8–11, with Kevin Douglas, Rachel Brand, and Nico Pantovich-Gonzalez in the lead roles. Audiences responded well — one theatergoer called it "really well done and very funny."

title: Spooky night for pets
copy: Halloween ranks second only to July 4th for stressed pets. Keep them inside with a quiet space, soft sounds, and treats — away from candy, decorations, and the constant doorbell. If you dress them up, keep it short.

title: Telluride Ski Resort hires new ski patrol director
copy: Telluride Ski Resort has named Elizabeth Howe as its new ski patrol director — a return for someone who started here as a liftie back in 1993. She spent 20 years at Telski before moving on to senior roles at Vail and Mountain Capital Partners. She stepped into the position in August.

title: SMPA pursues renewable energy purchase to secure long-term savings
copy: SMPA and three partner co-ops have agreed to purchase power from Valley Range Energy Park, a 125MW solar facility with battery storage planned east of Cortez, through Tri-State's BYOR program. If Montezuma County approves it, the project would cover roughly 40% of 2024 peak demand and save SMPA members around $5 million over 20 years.

title: Vote No on measure 5A
copy: Telluride School District spends over $36,600 per student — more than double the state average — while enrollment has dropped 20% and is projected to keep falling. Spending has climbed from $19M to $26.2M since 2021, and the promised cuts don't keep pace with inflation. Measure 5A asks local taxpayers for $2.7M annually for seven years.

title: What would it take?
copy: San Miguel Resource Center logged over 1,700 contacts with 125 domestic violence survivors in the past year. The recurring obstacles were housing, legal navigation, and access — not a lack of effort by survivors. No shelter exists in the service area, and getting help often depends on whether landlords, employers, and agencies are willing to cooperate.

title: Rule-breaking
copy: A Telluride family sent their 16-year-old daughter Vivian to the Alzar School — a semester program split between Cascade, Idaho and Patagonia, Chile — despite a longtime rule against boarding school. The school mixes academics with kayaking, backcountry expeditions, and wilderness training for a student body of 30. After 61 days apart, the family reunited for Family Weekend.

title: Post-apumpkalyptic
copy: Fall's a good time to step back from the pumpkin spice wave and try something quieter. Kitchari — rice, split mung dal, ghee, and simple spices — is an Ayurvedic staple valued for easy digestion and a grounding, warming quality. The piece also notes that pumpkin pie spice works fine in oatmeal, squash, or lentil soup if you've got it sitting around.

title: How can you not be romantic about baseball?
copy: Postseason baseball is here, and a longtime Dodger fan — attending games since 1964 — makes the case for why the sport still holds a unique place in American life. Telluride's own adult softball leagues draw some of the loudest crowds in Town Park, while flag football and basketball leagues don't exist here at all.

title: Employers invited to apply for employee housing master leases
copy: THA is accepting applications from local businesses, nonprofits, and government entities to master-lease units at the new Virginia Placer IIA building and the Boarding House. Applications are due in person by 11 a.m. on Oct. 28, with a lottery drawing set for Nov. 17. Leases start Dec. 1; rents range from $582/month for a Boarding House single room up to $3,147 for a two-bedroom apartment.

title: Dee Williams celebrated with volunteer honor
copy: Dee Williams has been named the Telluride Foundation's 2026 Volunteer of the Year, recognized for 50-plus years of service in Ouray County. She helped found the Home Trust of Ouray County, the Ouray Nordic Council, and played a key role in preserving the Wright Opera House. A community celebration is set for Nov. 10 at the Wright Opera House, 5–6:30 p.m.

title: Village Court Apartments waitlist to open on Oct. 27
copy: Mountain Village's housing authority is opening the waitlist for new units in VCA Building 16 on Oct. 27, noon–6 p.m., via an online form only. Units are 1BD/1BA or 2BD/2BA with full kitchens, W/D, and A/C; one parking pass per unit. Rent is income-based, up to 140% AMI.

title: Mountain Village adopts new outdoor lighting rules
copy: Mountain Village's updated outdoor lighting rules took effect July 16. Holiday lights are allowed Nov. 1–Jan. 31, must be off 10 p.m.–6 a.m., and can't flash. Most existing fixtures can stay for now, with compliance deadlines of 2031–2036 depending on type.

title: Warm up the bus
copy: Telluride's Lady Miners cross country team punched a full-squad ticket to the 2A State Championships after placing third at the Class 2A Region IV meet in Mancos. Juniors Ella Browne and Calliope Barber both shattered their personal records — each breaking 23 minutes for the first time — to secure the team's qualifying score. State runs October 31 in Colorado Springs.

title: 'Super Bowl for theater kids'
copy: THS theater students are raising $5,000 to attend ThesCon in Denver (Dec. 10–12) while staging "Young Frankenstein" Oct. 29–31 at the Michael D. Palm Theatre. Program ad sales and scholarships have covered about 20% so far. Funding cuts have hit the school's theater program hard since its drama teacher retired two years ago and wasn't replaced.

title: ‘Laugh-out-loud hilarious’
copy: Telluride Theatre and the Telluride School District are staging "Young Frankenstein" with 17 students in grades 7–12, running October 29–31 at the Michael D. Palm Theatre. Now in its second year of collaboration, the program includes student performers, designers, stage managers, and an assistant director.

title: Snow could shape winter air travel
copy: Flight bookings for this winter are running below recent seasons, with air service down 8% November through April compared to last year. Travelers are waiting on snowfall before committing to flights. Breeze's Orange County–Montrose route is paused, but United, American, Southwest, and Denver Airlines are all operating this winter.

title: Keeping warm on a frigid mountain
copy: Beacon Telluride is collecting gently used winter gear — jackets, gloves, base layers, hats, ski pants — for seasonal workers who may arrive underprepared for mountain cold. Drop-offs accepted at The Toggery through Nov. 15. The nonprofit also runs home-cooked meal hosting and other programs for seasonal employees all winter.

title: More flooding possible in Four Corners region after days of heavy rain
copy: Heavy rain since Wednesday has caused significant flooding across the Four Corners region, with rivers surging into homes and forcing evacuations — especially around Farmington, New Mexico. Saturated soils have a flood watch still in effect, with more storms expected. Officials warn returning residents of contaminated water, gas leaks, and other hazards.

title: Telluride Rewind
copy: Telluride's old town ordinances from 1966 included bans on opium dens, women loitering near saloons, and wearing clothing of the opposite sex. A 1981 council gave initial approval to convert the Nugget Theater into a 485-seat convention center. And in 1991, KOTO's Halloween bash drew 500-plus people and raised over $4,000.

title: Initial review of Shandoka parking structure approved by P&Z
copy: P&Z approved the preliminary PUD review for the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment, a proposed mixed-use project on the current surface parking lot that would include 50–60 housing units (80% deed-restricted affordable), a 900-vehicle parking structure, childcare, a food bank, and commercial space. The structure would replace 330 existing surface spots and absorb 288 spaces relocated from Carhenge. Some residents raised concerns about the added walking distance and traffic; HARC review continues Nov. 18.

title: Voters in 2 Democratic strongholds could ban transgender girls from girls school sports
copy: Voters in Colorado and Washington will decide ballot measures in 2026 to ban transgender girls from female school sports — the first time the question goes directly to voters rather than legislatures. Both states have Democratic-controlled governments that previously blocked such bans. Twenty-seven states already have these laws in place.

title: More rain is expected after bad flooding in the Four Corners region led to rescues and evacuations
copy: Severe flooding hit the Four Corners region this week, prompting 20 rescues, evacuations of 600 homes, and power outages for roughly 1,500 people in the Farmington and Shiprock areas. Four inches of rain fell on already-saturated ground Wednesday through Friday, with more expected. Southern Colorado saw flooding a full three feet above last year's 100-year flood level on the San Juan River.

title: Lottery for three-bedroom unit is open
copy: A deed-restricted 3-bed/2-bath condo at 226 East Pacific Avenue is up for lottery. Applications open Oct. 22 via SMRHA; submission window is Oct. 30–Nov. 20, with the drawing Dec. 11. Sale price is $453,000. Apply at smrha.org/applications — the window is short.

title: Chamberlain award winner Kingston featured at Bardic Trails
copy: Kate Kingston of Trinidad — a decorated Colorado poet with a long list of awards and fellowships — headlines Bardic Trails on Tuesday, Nov. 3 at 7 p.m. via Zoom. The free monthly series is hosted by Talking Gourds and open to all; the suggested prompt is "Dia de los Muertos." Visit tellurideinstitute.org/talking-gourds for the link.

title: A postcard from the Czech Republic
copy: Telluride High School sophomore Maddy Charleston is 11 months into a Rotary Youth Exchange in Jindřichův Hradec, Czech Republic — her first time traveling solo or outside the U.S. She's living with a host family, attending school, and picking up the language. The Telluride Rotary Club is also looking for a local family to host a Brazilian exchange student starting after the winter holidays.

title: Rooftop rescues and evacuations as severe flooding soaks Four Corners region
copy: Severe flooding hit the Four Corners region Friday, with rooftop rescues underway in San Juan County and some 600 Farmington households ordered to evacuate along the San Juan River. Southern Colorado saw flooding a full three feet above last year's 100-year flood event. More rain was forecast through the weekend.

title: 'We call it fellowship'
copy: AA meetings continue daily in Telluride at Christ Church, with a women's meeting resuming Thursdays at noon after an 18-month gap. Narcotics Anonymous meets Tuesdays at 5:30 p.m. Al-Anon recently ended its in-person run but online options remain via TellurideAlAnon@gmail.com.

title: Coffee and climate chats continue at the library
copy: A NOAA social scientist joins Sheep Mountain Alliance and EcoAction Partners Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8:30 a.m. at Wilkinson Public Library to talk about the anticipated "super El Niño" and what it might mean for the San Juans. The free Coffee & Climate Conversations series runs monthly. Tea, coffee, and pastries provided.

title: Here’s to your good health
copy: Uncompahgre Medical Center in Norwood is hosting a community forum Oct. 29, 6–8 p.m. at the Lone Cone Library to share plans for expanded primary care, at-home treatment, hospice services, and addiction medicine in the West End. UMC serves 66% of Norwood residents and ranks in the top 10% of Federally Qualified Health Centers nationally.

title: Expanding connections
copy: Lone Cone Library Director Kerry Bentler attended a rural libraries conference in Alabama on a scholarship from MacMillan Publishers, connecting with peers running operations closer to Norwood's scale. The library also has a new staff member, Daniella Pacheco-Rushing, and ongoing programs including a kids' STEAM series and weekly tech help sessions.

title: Spooky stagecraft
copy: Kindergarten through second-grade students from the Sheridan Arts Foundation's Young People's Theater will perform two Halloween-themed shows at the Sheridan Opera House on Oct. 28 at 5:15 p.m. — an adaptation of "The Little Ghost who was a Quilt" and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow." The Adventures in Acting program runs each spring and fall, enrolling more than 40 young students annually.

title: Agriculture secretary says agency is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service reorganization
copy: The Trump administration is pushing forward with a major Forest Service reorganization — moving headquarters to Salt Lake City, closing 23 research stations, and replacing regional offices with state offices — despite a federal judge's order halting the plan. The Forest Service workforce has already dropped roughly 16%, from 39,000 to 33,000 employees. The outcome is still in the courts.

title: Colorado, Utah communities flood as yet more moisture saturates US Southwest
copy: Heavy monsoon moisture hammered the Four Corners region Thursday — 80 homes and 50 RVs flooded in Hurricane, Utah, mandatory evacuations ordered along four rivers in southern Colorado including through Pagosa Springs, and Arizona saw multiple tornadoes the night before. Pagosa Springs officials expect crests a foot higher than last year's flood. NWS says the ground is saturated after three or four rounds of this pattern in recent weeks.

title: ‘We’re in a vast archaeological treasure trove’
copy: Rob Schultheis, a longtime Telluride resident and journalist, says he's been finding what he believes are Ice Age mammoth carvings across the valley for the past three years — in Lawson Hill, near Ames, near Ilium. He thinks they were hunting talismans, and says once you know what to look for, they're hard to miss.

title: Sister of American held in Russia says he didn't know he was being released until he saw US flag
copy: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired American teacher, was released from a Russian prison Wednesday after more than four years — he didn't know he was being freed until he saw a U.S. flag on the plane. His sister says he was starved and beaten during his imprisonment. He's expected to eventually settle in Colorado.

title: ‘Overjoyed just to get away’
copy: Little Pink Houses of Hope brought 12 breast-cancer families from across the country to Telluride for a weeklong retreat — the second year running. Fifteen local sponsors covered lodging, food, and activities, from wagon rides at Schmid Family Ranch on Wilson Mesa to a rainy-day Jeep trip to Bridal Veil Falls. For families like one from Houston whose kids had never left Texas, it was their first time in Colorado.

title: Norwood school construction raises noise concerns
copy: Construction of Norwood's new school near Pinion Park has drawn noise complaints from neighbors, mostly around early morning and holiday work. The town asks residents to report complaints directly to Town Hall at (970) 327-4288, not the school district. A traffic study also flagged sight-line issues at Grand Ave and South Market St., with crosswalks proposed but parking cuts drawing pushback from trustees.

title: Voting-related measures on November ballots include a voter ID push targeting mail-in ballots
copy: Voters in California, Colorado, and Nevada are deciding on ballot measures this November that would require driver's license or partial Social Security numbers on mail-in ballots. Similar measures appear in Arizona, North Carolina, and Ohio, referred by Republican-led legislatures. Nationally, about 1 in 5 state ballot measures this cycle touch voting rules or election procedures.

title: Spreading humanity through music
copy: Telluride-Boulder indie-folk duo LVDY performed for inmates in a Virginia jail addiction recovery program last April, and a video of the set racked up 4.5 million Instagram views. The pair are now fielding requests from other jail systems and plan to bring live music to more facilities on upcoming tours.

title: Legals and Public Notices for Oct. 22-28, 2026
copy: The Tomboy Lodge Association has filed a foreclosure on Unit 156A at 619 West Columbia Avenue in Telluride over an unpaid HOA balance of $15,449.81. A public auction is scheduled for December 16, 2026, at the San Miguel County Courthouse. A second notice involving The Good Gargoyle Condominiums was also published but cut off.

title: Cynthia Guy
copy: Cynthia "Cindy" Guy, 60, of Colorado passed away September 30, 2026. A massage therapist for over 30 years, she was known for her love of music, dancing, and the natural world. Donations in her memory may be made to Golden Retriever Rescue of the Rockies.

title: Sister of American Stephen Hubbard says he's in disbelief following release by Russia
copy: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired Michigan teacher held in a Russian prison since 2022, was released Wednesday following a call between President Trump and Putin. His sister says he endured beatings and starvation and now has an enlarged heart. He's headed home, and may settle in Colorado with family.

title: Local Employers Invited to Apply for Employee Housing Master Leases
copy: (October 22, 2026) – The Telluride Housing Authority (THA) is offering master leases on five apartments at the new Virginia Placer IIA building and two rooms at the Telluride Boarding House to local businesses and organizations.

title: Deed-Restricted Housing Lottery Applications Now Available for Spruce House H
copy: (October 22, 2026) - The Town of Telluride and the San Miguel Regional Housing Authority (SMRHA) opened applications today for a deed-restricted homeownership lottery for Spruce House H at 226 East Pacific Avenue, Unit H, Telluride, Colorado, 81435.

title: Black Bear and Imogene Passes Closed for the Winter
Second Annual Snowplow Naming Contest
Black Bear and Imogene Passes Closed for the Winter
copy: Due to changing weather conditions and the onset of winter, Imogene and Black Bear Passes are now officially closed for the season.
